_comment: Written by the Security Review persona. The pre-tag CI job reads this to decide whether a release is covered by a current audit. Do not hand-edit.
open_findings: RESOLVED #151, verified by execution rather than by reading the diff. The scenario that defined the finding was re-run on this tree: with scripts/rotate-inbound-webhook.py migrated to /v2/webhooks, 8aa9f7a returned exit 0 / all PASS with a live GET /v1/webhooks in the shipped bundle; 9cbcc87 returns exit 2 with WARN 'no deliberate sunsetting calls remain: 1 deliberate call(s) still in the tree, nearest sunset in 157 days: zaf-build/assets/background.html:91'. The closure is structural, not scenario-specific: a v1 call in the tree is now either marked, which produces the deliberate WARN, or unmarked, which produces the sunsetting WARN or FAIL, so exit 0 requires that no v1 call exists at all. Escalation boundary probed across the flip rather than at a point: 92d WARN, 91d WARN, 90d FAIL, 89d FAIL, and the superseded branch is the exact complement of the excusing branch, so no run reads one call as both deliberate and escalating. Condition 6 probed adversarially with expiries of 2027-01-01, 2099-01-01 and 9999-12-31: none defers the 2026-10-03 escalation, because the window is computed from the entry's sunset and not from the marker's date.

RESOLVED #155, verified by execution. tsanetGet was extracted verbatim from both revisions of zaf-build/assets/background.html and driven under a login that always succeeds against an endpoint that always 401s. Pre-fix (8aa9f7a) the chain was still climbing at 50,000 logins and 50,000 GETs when an artificial cap stopped it. Post-fix (9cbcc87) it rejects after exactly 2 logins and 2 GETs with 'TSANet GET failed: 401', so the rejection reaches the caller's .catch and setInterval no longer accumulates non-terminating chains. The guard mirrors main.js.

MEDIUM (on #144, not filed separately): no release exists. v1.0.54 is still the newest tag and the newest GitHub Release; the manifest at 9cbcc87 reads 1.0.57. Both #148/#149 and now #159 are in main and in no installable artifact. Re-verified this round: `git show v1.0.54:zaf-build/assets/background.html` still carries the fail-open probe at line 73 AND the unguarded 401 retry, so members today run the two conditions #148 and #159 exist to remove. Nothing in this delta argues against cutting the release; the delta strictly improves the shipped bundle.

MEDIUM #152: the excused call still fails the marker's own admission test. #159 added the expiry but did not change ALLOW_MARKER's contract line, which still reads 'Every use is a claim that the call survives its sunset', nor the call-site justification at background.html:89-90, which still says the v1 call 'is expected to fail after 2027-01-01, and the v2 one below answers in its place'. That second half remains false for the reason the same file gives fifteen lines earlier: `_pushRegistered = found || !complete` is constant true once complete is permanently false, so the v2 answer is discarded rather than substituted. #159 makes the marker expire on the sunset date, which bounds the damage, but the two contradictory statements are both still in the file.

MEDIUM #153: the residual v1 probe call is still tracked by nothing other than this issue. Unchanged by #159, which was the right scope. #101's ZAF workstream covers the collaboration-request list migration, which shipped; its Subscriptions workstream covers members' own subscriptions; Connect-ReleaseMGT#210's connector table still lists only the Quick Start registration and rotate-inbound-webhook.py for this repo. The marker at background.html:91 still cites no issue, so the marker and its tracker remain unlinked.
MEDIUM #154: partner-controlled fieldId interpolated unescaped into an innerHTML sink at main.js:858 and 860. Untouched by this delta and unchanged.
LOW #156: sanitizeHtml's allowlist consults the prototype chain. Untouched by this delta.
LOW #157: stripHtml decodes entities after stripping tags. Untouched by this delta.

MEDIUM #158, RAISED FROM LOW THIS ROUND on Shawn's go, because #159 changed what it composes with. As filed it is a refactor hazard with a canary: rewriting baseUrl's default from `(version || 'v1')` to a ternary turns on_v1_base false and gates off both needs_v1_base patterns, but a marker left behind still fires the stale-marker WARN. Probed on this tree: [1] baseline exit 2; [2] ternary rewrite with the marker left in place, exit 2, stale-marker WARN names the file; [3] ternary rewrite with the marker removed in the same edit, exit 2, and the shipped v1 call is invisible, the only remaining WARN coming from rotate-inbound-webhook.py; [4] the same tree with rotate-inbound-webhook.py also migrated to v2, which is #101's declared scope: exit 0, 17 PASS, 0 warn, 0 fail, with `tsanetGet('/webhooks')` still at background.html:91 and still in the bundle members install. That is the exact end state #151 described, reached by a different route that #159 does not close and did not claim to. The route is narrow and needs three independent changes, but two of the three are planned work. #158's own recorded fix closes it: assert the anchor rather than infer it, failing if no file under zaf-build/ matches v1_base. Raised to medium-priority 2026-07-29 with the probe table posted as a comment on the issue. It therefore joins the blocking set; see the gate note.

LOW #160, FILED 2026-07-29: the suite can print a PASS whose text is false while an adjacent WARN carries the truth. With the marker valid and rotate-inbound-webhook.py migrated, one run prints `PASS no calls to sunsetting endpoints - no known-deprecated endpoint usage found` and `WARN no deliberate sunsetting calls remain - 1 deliberate call(s) still in the tree ... background.html:91`. A deprecated call is in the tree, so the PASS line is not true as written. The exit code is 2 and release.yml keys on the exit code, so no gate is misled, and the WARN names the file and line. This is the same defect class #159 deliberately avoided for the superseded branch, where its comment reasons that reporting one call twice would 'put two lines about one call in the same run saying opposite things'. The same reasoning was not applied to the PASS. FIX: when marked calls exist, make the sunsetting check say so rather than say nothing was found, or fold both into one record.
MEDIUM #140: an uncovered release is easy to accept repeatedly. OPEN, accepted by Shawn 2026-07-28.
MEDIUM #96: durable audit trail. OPEN, accepted.
MEDIUM #119: move the ZAF app off the TSANet API user password to the ZIS Entra client credential. OPEN, accepted.
LOW #98: note attribution heuristic remains open pending Connect-API-Code#131. OPEN, accepted.
notes: Extends the record from 8aa9f7a to 9cbcc87 (manifest 1.0.57; neither 1.0.56 nor 1.0.57 is in any release). The delta is five commits, four of which edit this record. The only source change is 9cbcc87, the squash of #159: scripts/security-audit.py +157, zaf-build/assets/background.html +12, manifest 1.0.56 -> 1.0.57. .github/ and zis/ are untouched, confirmed by `git diff --name-only 8aa9f7a..9cbcc87` over the watched set.

SELF_REVIEWED IS TRUE, AND THE SHAPE OF IT IS DIFFERENT THIS ROUND, so it is stated rather than left to the flag. This reviewer did not write #159, but did run the QA rounds on it, and rounds two and three of that QA are what produced two of the fixes now under security review: the unguarded fromisoformat that let a typo abort the audit at exit 3, and the malformed expiry that reported as 'no expiry' on a line visibly reading `until`. So this pass is grading whether its own review demands were adequately met. That is weaker than reviewing code one wrote, and it is not independence, because the reviewer has a prior position on what the right fix looked like. Every earlier QA conclusion was therefore re-derived by execution on this tree rather than carried: the closure scenarios, the escalation boundary, all four marker-validation paths, and the 401 guard were each re-run from scratch. Where a claim could only be confirmed by reading, it is listed as NOT VERIFIED below. This record still carries the standing request for a second signer, and it applies more strongly here than to a pure self-review of prose.

BOTH CLAIMED CLOSURES VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING THE DIFF. #151: the defining scenario flips from exit 0 / all PASS at 8aa9f7a to exit 2 with the call named at 9cbcc87. #155: tsanetGet extracted verbatim from each revision and driven against a permanent 401, 50,000+ logins pre-fix versus exactly 2 post-fix. Details in open_findings.

THE THREE-WAY DIAGNOSIS WORKS AND EACH PATH FAILS CLOSED, probed individually on the shipped marker line. Undated: FAIL, 'has no `until <YYYY-MM-DD>` expiry, so it excuses nothing'. Malformed (`until soon`): FAIL, 'has a malformed expiry, expected `until <YYYY-MM-DD>`'. Right shape but not a real date (`2026-02-30`): FAIL, 'the right shape but not a real date', at exit 1 rather than the exit 3 abort the unguarded parse produced. Expired: FAIL, naming the date. All four exit 1, all four name file and line, none aborts the suite, and none excuses its call. Two adversarial orderings were also probed: an undated marker followed by a valid one on the same line FAILs, which is the safe direction, and a second `audit-allow:` with no comment opener of its own is not a marker at all.

#151's ACCEPTANCE, ITEM BY ITEM. (1) A marker without an expiry is rejected: MET, verified. (2) With rotate-inbound-webhook.py migrated and background.html unchanged, the suite does not exit 0 and the marked call is still reported: MET, verified, exit 2 with file and line. (3) today=2026-10-03 produces a non-PASS on this tree even after that migration: MET, verified FAIL. (4) .security-audit.json records the count and location of marked-but-shipping calls: NOT met by #159, which changed no record; it is met by THIS record, in the new `marked_calls` field. Stated plainly because #159 closed #151 with that criterion outstanding, and a closed issue whose acceptance is completed elsewhere should say where.

WHAT #159 DID NOT CLOSE, AND DID NOT CLAIM TO. The end state #151 named, exit 0 with a live v1 call in the shipped bundle, is still reachable at 9cbcc87 through #158's anchor loss composed with #101's planned migration of rotate-inbound-webhook.py. Probed to exit 0 / 17 PASS / 0 warn with the call still at background.html:91. #159 closes the marker route completely; it does not close the class. See #158 in open_findings, with the recommendation to raise its severity.

THE SHIPPED CHANGE IS FOUR LINES IN THE AUTH PATH OF EVERY BACKGROUND CALL, so it was checked beyond the guard itself. The signature becomes tsanetGet(path, version, retried); all four call sites in the file pass (path) or (path, version) and none passes a third argument, so nothing binds `retried` accidentally. NOTED, not a finding: main.js uses tsanetGet(path, retried, version) while background.html now uses tsanetGet(path, version, retried). Each file is internally consistent, but the orders are transposed, so a call copied between files would silently bind version to a boolean. Worth aligning next time either file is touched.

CATEGORIES WITH NO DELTA, stated as no-delta rather than as clean, because the previous round's failure was marking a category clean after declining to review it. Category 1: re-verified independently on this tree anyway, since the release gate reads this file. All three Actions pinned to full 40-char SHAs; all four workflows declare permissions, release.yml with {} at workflow scope; SRI recomputed by fetching zaf_sdk 2.0.37 and hashing it, matching the integrity attribute in all three HTML files; secret scan across js/json/html/py clean; domainWhitelist still exactly the two connect2 hosts; tsanet_password still the only secure parameter. The release finding remains open and is Category 1's. Categories 3, 4, 5: no delta. The delta adds no endpoint, no destination, no field, no permission and no log statement; the only behavioural change is that a 401 retry now stops after one attempt. Category 7: NO DELTA AND NOT RE-REVIEWED THIS ROUND. #154, #156 and #157 remain open and unchanged; nothing here should be read as re-clearing them. Category 2 and Category 6 are where this delta lives and are covered above.

GATE CONSEQUENCE OF ADVANCING TO 9cbcc87, which is the point of writing this. COVERED becomes true: the mechanical suite exits 2, which release.yml classifies as 'warnings only' and not a coverage flag; the record parses; 9cbcc87 is an ancestor of any tag cut from main; and `git diff --name-only 9cbcc87..HEAD -- zaf-build/ zis/ scripts/ .github/workflows/` is empty, so committing this record does not itself create drift, because .security-audit.json is outside the watched set. FLAGGED stays true, and the blocking set GREW this round rather than shrank: #144 (high), #152, #153, #154 and now #158 (medium) are open, labelled security and NOT accepted, so release.yml's findings check flags on FIVE issues. #158 was low-priority and skipped before this review raised it; raising it is what moved it into the blocking set, and that is a deliberate consequence rather than a side effect. #98, #156, #157 and the newly filed #160 are low-priority, reported and do not flag. #96, #98, #119 and #140 remain accepted and unchanged; NOTHING was accepted by this review. Cutting the release therefore requires accepting five issues explicitly, and #144 still cannot close until the release it blocks exists. Simulated against the live issue list with release.yml's own query and this record's accepted_issues: BLOCKING #144 high-priority, #152, #153, #154, #158 medium-priority; ACCEPTED #96, #119, #140; SKIPPED #98, #156, #157, #160.

THE DELIBERATE CALL IS A WARN, NOT A FAIL, AND THAT IS BY DESIGN BUT WORTH NAMING. release.yml treats exit 2 as 'warnings only', so the one marked v1 call in the shipped bundle is visible on the run page and does not mark the build uncovered. #151 asked for exactly this ('does not exit 0 and the marked call is still reported'), so it is the requested behaviour rather than a gap. It becomes a FAIL on 2026-10-03 whatever the marker says.

SCHEDULED TIGHTENING, carried forward and now more reliable than when it was written. From 2026-10-03 check_deprecated_endpoints() returns FAIL and the coverage gate flags. The previous record's caveat, that a marked call could silently defeat this, no longer holds for the marker route: probed at 90 days, the marker is withdrawn and the call becomes a finding regardless of its expiry. The caveat does still hold for the #158 route.

NOT VERIFIED, carried and updated. Still open from previous rounds: whether TSANet storage permits a non-integer fieldId to reach a client; what status GET /v1/webhooks returns after removal (404, 410 or 401, and a 401 would still enter the retry path, though now bounded at one retry); release.yml's behaviour under a FAILING audit, still read and never exercised, and reachable on 2026-10-03; #138's fix, verified by inspection and by the mechanical check, not by pushing a hostile tag; PROD runtime, PROD credentials known-dead; whether GuardCreate (#41) absorbs the duplicate condition the v1.0.54 fail-open path creates today; the docx, ZIS Quick Start and GitBook surfaces. NEW this round: the audit script's other checks (SRI, pinning, permissions, expression injection, embedded secrets, secure settings) were not re-probed by mutation the way check_deprecated_endpoints was, so their correctness rests on reading plus their PASS output; no live BETA or Zendesk probe was run this round, because the delta touches no endpoint; and the marker mechanism was probed against the shipped marker line only, not against every file the walker visits.

RESOLVED AND DROPPED FOR CAUSE this round: #151 and #155, both by execution, both recorded above rather than deleted. Nothing else left the list. The three items the previous record resolved stay resolved.

FILED 2026-07-29 on Shawn's go, from this review: #160 (low), the PASS line that reads 'no known-deprecated endpoint usage found' while a marked v1 call is in the tree. And #158 raised from low-priority to medium-priority, with the four-step probe table posted as a comment so the severity change carries its evidence rather than an assertion. Both actions were authorised explicitly; no issue was accepted, no tag cut, no release made.

sites: zaf-build/assets/background.html:91 - GET /v1/webhooks, marker `audit-allow: v1-webhooks until 2027-01-01`, sunset 2027-01-01, shipped in the bundle members install. Reported by the suite as a WARN on every run. Deleting it is tracked by #153.
